implementation_notes: There is no circular buffer in the BCL, so this is either a hand-written class (a T[] with two indices, using Interlocked for the acquire/release on the indices) or a bounded BlockingCollection/Channel if blocking is acceptable. For a high-throughput SPSC ring, the hand-written version with Interlocked.Read/Write and a power-of-two mask plus padding ([StructLayout(LayoutKind.Sequential)] with explicit padding fields or a layout that puts the indices on separate lines) is the way; .NET's memory model guarantees release on a Volatile.Write and acquire on a Volatile.Read, and Interlocked gives the full fence when needed. For the general case System.Threading.Channels.Channel<T> (bounded capacity) is a better fit because it handles multiple producers and consumers, blocking, and cancellation correctly. Avoid Array.Resize for a 'growing ring' - that reallocates and copies, which is the copying the ring exists to avoid.
idiom_name: hand-written SPSC ring with Interlocked/Volatile indices; Channel<T> (bounded) for the general blocking case
pitfalls: Volatile.Read/Write give visibility and the acquire/release ordering, but they are NOT a read-modify-write - never do head++ on a plain field and assume Volatile saves it.
head - tail == Capacity as the full test is only correct with monotonic long counters; masking head itself breaks it.
The head and tail must be on separate cache lines (padding) or the ping-pong dominates and a lock is faster.
Array.Resize is not a growing ring - it reallocates and copies, which is the copying the ring removes.
For MPMC or blocking, use Channel<T> (bounded) rather than adapting this SPSC class, which is only correct for one producer and one consumer.
